assets.title: Vascular territories, medulla (ASA vs PICA)
assets.source: Brazis p. 441, Vascular Supply of the Medulla
notes: Book: paramedian bulbar branches (vertebral artery, ASA at lower levels) vs lateral bulbar branches (intracranial vertebral artery or PICA).
The inferior olive is assigned to PICA in the app; the extracted text does not state the olive's supply.

assets.title: Vascular territories, pons (basilar paramedian vs AICA)
assets.source: Brazis p. 447-448, Vascular Supply of the Pons
notes: Book: paramedian vessels supply the medial basal pons (pontine nuclei, corticospinal fibres, medial lemniscus); AICA supplies the lateral tegmentum of the lower two-thirds of the pons.

Possible inconsistency: the vascular map puts the abducens nucleus and MLF in the basilar paramedian territory, while the Foville card says 'circumferential branches' for a lesion involving the abducens nucleus. Check against the book.

assets.title: Vascular territories, midbrain (peduncular vs quadrigeminal)
assets.source: Brazis p. 452, Vascular Supply of the Mesencephalon
notes: Corrected against the extracted text (p. 452). Paramedian vessels (retromamillary trunk from the PCA origins): thalamoperforating arteries supply the thalamus; peduncular arteries supply the medial peduncles and the midbrain tegmentum, including the oculomotor nucleus, red nucleus and substantia nigra.
Circumferential: quadrigeminal arteries supply the superior and inferior colliculi. The app no longer assigns the red nucleus to the thalamoperforating territory.

The medial lemniscus, spinothalamic tract and periaqueductal gray were removed from the quadrigeminal territory because the book does not assign them to an artery in this section; they are shown without a territory.
AI-checked against the text only; the clinical review is the owner's.

assets.title: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg)
notes: Atlas card cites pp. 443-446 and the matrix has no page; the first text mention is on p. 441. Verify pages.
Matrix key clue says 'ZERO limb motor weakness'; confirm the wording against the book.

assets.title: Medial medullary (Dejerine)
notes: Atlas card cites pp. 441-443. Extracted text: the ASA supplies the ipsilateral pyramid, medial lemniscus and hypoglossal nerve/nucleus (matches the card).

assets.title: Submedullary (Opalski)
notes: Text matches: lateral medullary syndrome plus ipsilateral hemiplegia from caudal extension below the pyramidal decussation (vertebral artery steno-occlusion or dissection).

assets.title: Millard-Gubler (ventral caudal pons)
notes: App cites pp. 449-450 for the atlas card (exact printed page: p. 448).
Content matches: contralateral hemiplegia sparing the face, ipsilateral lateral rectus paresis, ipsilateral peripheral facial paresis.

assets.title: Raymond (ventral medial pons)
notes: App cites p. 450 (extracted text: p. 448).

Content matches (ipsilateral VI, contralateral hemiplegia with central facial paresis). The book adds that later observations challenged the facial involvement and described conjugate gaze palsy from abducens nucleus lesions; the app states facial sparing as fact and omits this.
The book also describes Raymond-Cestan syndrome (p. 449): ipsilateral INO, contralateral cerebellar signs with rubral tremor, contralateral hypesthesia. It is not in the app.

assets.title: Foville (dorsal caudal pontine tegmentum)
notes: App cites p. 450 (exact printed page: p. 449).

Content matches: contralateral hemiplegia with facial sparing, ipsilateral peripheral facial palsy, ipsilateral conjugate gaze palsy (PPRF/abducens nucleus). Do not confuse it with the 'midbrain syndrome of Foville' (p. 452).

assets.title: Marie-Foix (lateral pons, brachium pontis)
notes: Text (p. 449): lateral pontine lesions, especially of the brachium pontis: ipsilateral cerebellar ataxia, contralateral hemiparesis, variable contralateral hemihypesthesia for pain and temperature.

Removed 'occasional CN VII / VIII' (not in the text; Ch. 15 only mentions CN VII/VIII in the 'sixteen-and-a-half syndrome', p. 450, unrelated) and the vessel 'AICA / lateral pontine branches' (Brazis names no vessel). The flowchart still draws AICA -> Marie-Foix and now labels the vessel as not stated by Brazis.

assets.title: Locked-in syndrome (bilateral basis pontis)
notes: Text (pp. 448-449): bilateral ventral pontine lesions (many causes; basilar artery thrombosis may progress to it). Quadriplegia, aphonia, 'occasional' impairment of horizontal eye movements (bilateral CN VI fascicles). Reticular formation spared (fully awake); vertical eye movements and blinking intact.

Fixed: 'occasional' qualifier restored; 'SRAA' removed (reticular formation spared stated in English); 'communicates exclusively with vertical eye movements' replaced by the book's wording (vertical eye movements and blinking); vessel no longer limited to 'mid-basilar occlusion'; 'preserved sensation' removed (not stated).

assets.title: Weber (ventral midbrain, crus cerebri)
notes: App cites p. 452. Content matches: contralateral hemiplegia including lower facial weakness, ipsilateral oculomotor paresis with dilated pupil.
Removed the unsupported absolute 'tremor, ataxia are completely absent'; the matrix now states the contrast with the tegmental syndromes.

assets.title: Benedikt (midbrain tegmentum, red nucleus)
notes: Ch. 15 (p. 453): ipsilateral oculomotor paresis (usually dilated pupil), contralateral hemiataxia with intention tremor due to red nucleus destruction, contralateral hemiparesis with hyperactive stretch reflexes; usually a consequence of infarcted PCA branches.

Ch. 8 (p. 214 and Table 8-8): larger lesions of the fascicle and red nucleus-substantia nigra region produce oculomotor palsy with contralateral choreiform movements or tremor. So chorea IS in Brazis, but only in Ch. 8; the unsupported terms 'athetosis', 'choreoathetosis', 'hyperkinesia', 'coarse' and 'variable medial lemniscus impairment' were removed.
Vessel changed from 'thalamoperforating' to 'branches of the PCA' (red nucleus: peduncular arteries, p. 452).
Page citations corrected from 453-454 to 453 (Ch. 15).

assets.title: Claude (dorsal midbrain tegmentum)
notes: Ch. 15 (p. 453): 'similar clinical manifestations' to Benedikt from a more dorsal tegmental lesion injuring the dorsal red nucleus and brachium conjunctivum, with prominent cerebellar signs (asynergia, ataxia, dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia) and no hemiballismus.
Ch. 8 (p. 214): fascicular involvement plus red nucleus and superior cerebellar peduncle damage cause contralateral ataxia and outflow-tract cerebellar tremor (Claude syndrome).
Removed: 'pure' cerebellar ataxia, 'NO tremor or chorea' (contradicted by Ch. 8), 'SCP decussation' (not stated), 'no significant hemiparesis' and the vessel 'PCA / SCA' (not stated).
Page citation corrected from 454 to 453.

assets.title: Parinaud (dorsal midbrain / Sylvian aqueduct)
notes: App cited pp. 454-456; corrected to p. 453. Content matches: upward gaze paralysis (occasionally down-gaze), large pupils with light-near dissociation, convergence-retraction nystagmus, Collier sign.
